headline: The Select Board reviewed plans for a $40 million Route 9 sewer system, while town boards advanced conservation rules and development reviews.
synopsis: The Select Board extended the Regional Wastewater Planning Committee charge to June 2027 as the town prepares a financing district for a proposed $40 million to $50 million Route 9 wastewater system. The board also reviewed long-term funding strategies for retiree health liabilities and expanded the Senior Tax Work-Off program to 40 positions. The Conservation Commission adopted updated rules for town conservation properties and continued review of a two-building apartment proposal at 0 Southville Road. Meanwhile, the Planning Board penalized an unauthorized public tree removal on Route 9 and began drafting native planting standards for future site plans.

highlights.title: Route 9 wastewater system update and committee extension
highlights.why: The Regional Wastewater Planning Committee outlined plans for a $40 million to $50 million sewer system along Route 9, and the Select Board voted 4-0-1 to extend the committee's work through June 2027.

highlights.title: OPEB actuarial valuation and funding strategy
highlights.why: Actuaries reported that Southborough's retiree health trust holds about $4.5 million, an 8 percent funded ratio, prompting discussions on redirecting regional pension funds once that system is fully funded around 2036.

highlights.title: 0 Southville Road apartment development review
highlights.why: The Conservation Commission reviewed a notice of intent for two apartment buildings involving roughly 4,500 square feet of riverfront disturbance and continued the hearing for peer review.

highlights.title: Unauthorized tree removal mitigation at 154 Turnpike Road
highlights.why: After a developer removed a 24-inch public shade tree without permission, the Planning Board and Tree Warden approved remediation requiring the developer to provide six replacement trees to the town.

highlights.title: Adoption of town conservation land use regulations
highlights.why: The Conservation Commission voted to formally adopt updated regulations governing municipal conservation land under Section 43-2 of the Town Code.

highlights.title: Senior Tax Work-Off program expansion
highlights.why: The Select Board approved revisions to the Senior Tax Work-Off Policy, streamlining eligibility and increasing the maximum number of participant positions from 30 to 40.
